title: llm-prefetch-routing-ideas-priya-ramesh
summary: Brainstorm / parking-lot for KV-prefetch + routing features to reduce tail latency and token cost. Rough ideas, tradeoffs, and experiments to try.
content:
Context:
- Goal: reduce p50/p95/P99 latency for multi-turn chat workloads while keeping token cost low. Need feature set that can be productized (configurable, safe fallbacks).
- Current levers: batching, quantization, model routing, KV cache reuse. Prefetch KV on likely next-turn prompts looks promising for chat-heavy apps.

Open questions / assumptions:
- How predictable are next-turn tokens? For assistant-style chat, user replies are often short, certain classes more predictable (yes/no, small clarifying Qs). For multi-turn docs/editing, unpredictable.
- Cost tradeoff: prefetching incurs compute for tokens that might not be used. Need hit-rate targets to justify.
- Privacy/PII: prefetching uses recent context — ensure private deployments respect KMS/HSM policies and audit logs.

Feature ideas (rough):
1) Adaptive KV-prefetch (client + runtime)
   - Client signals: user-intent hints (e.g., end-of-turn intent=confirm/edit/ask) or UI events (user typing pause, cursor location) to trigger prefetch.
   - Runtime component: for a given session, build a small predictive model (lightweight) that scores next-token prefix likelihood. If score > threshold, prefetch KV into warm pool.
   - Config: prefetch_budget (tokens/sec), prefetch_threshold, decay window, allowed_models for prefetch.
   - Fall back: if prefetch fails or predicted tokens differ, continue cold path. Metrics: prefetch hit-rate, cost per saved-ms, percent of requests with reduced cold-start lat.

2) Tiered routing with prefetch-aware routing
   - Maintain model variants: fast-quantized (Q4), baseline (FP16), high-quality. Route predicted-prefetch sessions to fast-quantized variants where cached KV leads to acceptable quality.
   - If runtime sees mismatch quality signals (eval hooks), route subsequent turns to higher-quality variant.

3) User-level caches + selective invalidation
   - Cache KV by session + prompt-template signature. Allow TTL and explicit invalidation (client-driven).
   - Make cache inspectable in Console (for debugging): show cache hits, evictions, keys.

4) Prefetch orchestration UI (Console)
   - Recommend prefetch configs per app based on traffic patterns (RL-style: suggest thresholds, expected cost delta).
   - A/B control: can enable prefetch for X% of sessions.

Experimentation plan (MVP):
- Week 1: implement a server-side synthetic prefetch simulator. Replay production traces (anonymized) and simulate greedy prefetch of n next tokens based on simple heuristics (most-common-next-token from N-gram on prompt templates). Compute hit-rate vs extra tokens used.
- Week 2: small runtime prototype that can precompute KV for top-1 predicted continuation per session and store in warm pool for 10s. Route a small traffic sample (1%) and measure p50/p95 improvement and delta cost.
- Week 3: add client opt-in flags and console toggle, run A/B for 2 weeks, collect quality regressions via eval set + live metrics.

Risks / Mitigations:
- Wasted compute -> set strict budget and conservative thresholds; start with user cohorts where next-turn distribution is predictable (e.g., transactional bots).
- Privacy concerns -> ensure private deployments opt-out or use customer-only keying; add audit logging for prefetch events.
- Complexity of routing + rollout -> start with routing disabled; enable prefetch only for same-model variants to avoid cross-model compatibility issues.

Notes / To-dos:
- Talk to Applied ML (Noah) about quick predictor prototype (lightweight LSTM/transformer20) or simpler n-gram baseline.
- Add cost model: estimate GPU-seconds per prefetched token and compare to token-cost of cold lat reduction. Need SRE input on warm pool sizing.
- Link to INF-987 (Jira) and CONFLUENCE-1234 for prior kv-prefetch notes.
- Draft API sketch: POST /v1/sessions/:id/prefetch {hint: "typing", budget_tokens: 16, max_latency_ms: 50} -> 202 accepted.

Rough product requirements (for PRD later):
- Configurable prefetch policies (global, per-app, per-route)
- Metrics surfaced in Console (prefetch hits / misses, cost delta, latency improvements)
- Safe rollout controls and canarying
- SDK client helpers for web/desktop apps to signal intent

Ideas for future (parking lot):
- Collaborative prefetch across users for public chatrooms (shared context) — privacy concerns though.
- ML-based routing that jointly optimizes batching + prefetch decisions.
- Prefetch for embeddings-heavy flows (precompute embeddings for likely next queries).

Slack threads / tickets to reference:
- #runtime-optimizations 2025-11-10 (prefetch convo)
- JIRA-INF-987 (warm-pool infra)

Immediate ask (from me):
- Aisha: can you share anonymized session traces we can replay?
- Noah: rough sketch of a predictor model we can run offline on traces?
- SRE: ballpark warm-pool memory/slot cost for holding prefetched KV for 10s on a p4-equivalent instance?

End notes: rough and messy — saving here so I can iterate into a PRD once we have replay results. Will refine API sketch and metrics next.
